messages.content: The organizer moved the first meeting to 8:45 Thursday morning, so drop the same-day flight. Compare the Wednesday evening option with downtown hotels near the office. The reimbursable hotel limit is $285 including tax.

Understood. I’ll use the Wednesday, May 13 nonstop from ORD at 7:10 p.m., arriving MSP at 8:42 p.m., and compare nearby hotels on all-in cost, airport arrival practicality, walking time to the office, and cancellation terms. I’ll also check Thursday returns departing after 4:00 p.m. Nothing will be booked.
The office is at 80 South Eighth Street. Keep the list short.

I found three practical one-night choices for May 13, all within the $285 reimbursement limit:

Hampton Inn & Suites Minneapolis/Downtown: $262 including tax, about an 8-minute walk to 80 South Eighth Street. Free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. on May 12; after that, one night is charged.

Hyatt Centric Downtown Minneapolis: $284 including tax, about a 4-minute walk. Free cancellation until 11:59 p.m. on May 11; after that, one night is charged.

Hilton Garden Inn Minneapolis Downtown: $246 including tax, about a 14-minute walk. Free cancellation until 11:59 p.m. on May 11; after that, one night is charged.

The Hampton has the best balance of price, walk, and cancellation flexibility. The Hyatt is closest but uses nearly the full allowance. The Hilton saves $16 versus the Hampton, but adds roughly six minutes each way on foot.
How practical is the Hampton after that flight? I don’t want the room savings erased by an awkward transfer.

It is straightforward. With an 8:42 p.m. scheduled arrival, a typical rideshare pickup after deplaning should be around 9:05 to 9:15. The drive to the Hampton is usually 20 to 25 minutes at that hour, putting you at the hotel around 9:30 to 9:40. Estimated fare is $30 to $36 before tip.

The light rail is cheaper at about $2.50, but it requires a roughly 10-minute walk from the downtown station to the hotel and would likely put arrival closer to 9:50. For this schedule, rideshare is the cleaner comparison.
Use rideshare in the totals. What returns are realistic if the review could end anywhere from 2:30 to 4:15?

Two nonstop returns fit different ending times:

MSP-ORD at 4:55 p.m., arriving 6:27 p.m. The round-trip fare with the Wednesday outbound is $361. To allow for the downtown drive and airport security, I would leave the office by 3:20 p.m. That works if the review ends by about 2:45, but not if it runs later.

MSP-ORD at 6:20 p.m., arriving 7:52 p.m. The round-trip fare remains $329. Leaving the office around 4:40 p.m. is reasonable, so a 4:15 finish still leaves a modest buffer.

Both are standard economy fares: nonrefundable, but cancellable before departure for an airline credit, with no change fee apart from any fare difference.
So the later flight is cheaper as well?
Yes. The 6:20 p.m. return makes the round trip $32 less than the 4:55 p.m. return. Its only disadvantage is getting back to Chicago 85 minutes later.
Give me the full Hampton totals for both returns.

Using the Hampton and estimated rideshares in Minneapolis:

Earlier-return plan: $361 airfare + $262 hotel + $66 ground transportation = $689 total. This assumes about $33 from MSP to the hotel and $33 from the office to MSP.

Later-return plan: $329 airfare + $262 hotel + $66 ground transportation = $657 total.

Both totals are within the hotel reimbursement limit and exclude travel between your home and ORD. The later return costs $32 less overall.
Compare the Hyatt too. Four minutes is useful if the morning is tight.

With the same $66 rideshare estimate, the Hyatt combinations are $711 with the 4:55 p.m. return and $679 with the 6:20 p.m. return. That is $22 more than the equivalent Hampton plans.

The Hyatt saves about four minutes of walking in the morning and is slightly simpler for reaching the office. Its tradeoff is the earlier cancellation deadline: Monday night, May 11, versus 6:00 p.m. Tuesday, May 12, at the Hampton.
Is the $284 Hyatt rate definitely reimbursable, or is there some separate destination fee?

The quoted $284 is the complete room total for one night, including taxes. No destination or facility fee is listed, so it fits under the $285 reimbursable amount by $1. Parking is not included, but it does not apply to this plan.
Then the Hilton isn’t compelling. Remove it.
Removed. It only saved $16 against the Hampton while adding a longer walk and offering the same Monday-night cancellation cutoff as the Hyatt.
I’m leaning Hampton with the 6:20 return, but the organizer says the ending time will be confirmed tomorrow. Is there any reason to hold the 4:55 instead?

Only if getting home earlier matters enough to justify the extra $32 and the risk of a rushed airport transfer. The 4:55 return requires a firm finish around 2:45; even a 3:15 ending would make it uncomfortable. The 6:20 return accommodates the full stated range through 4:15 and costs less.

Because both airfares are currently available and neither option is being booked now, there is no operational advantage to choosing the 4:55 before the organizer confirms the schedule.
Keep two complete combinations anyway: the closest hotel with the early return, and the better-value hotel with the later return. Spell out the deadlines so I can decide quickly tomorrow.

I’ll retain these two unbooked combinations:

Early-finish combination: Wednesday ORD-MSP 7:10-8:42 p.m.; Hyatt Centric Downtown Minneapolis at $284 including tax, 4-minute walk to the office; Thursday MSP-ORD 4:55-6:27 p.m. Airfare is $361 and estimated Minneapolis rideshares are $66, for a projected total of $711. Leave the office by 3:20 p.m. The hotel is cancellable without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Monday, May 11.

Later-finish combination: the same Wednesday outbound; Hampton Inn & Suites Minneapolis/Downtown at $262 including tax, 8-minute walk; Thursday MSP-ORD 6:20-7:52 p.m. Airfare is $329 and estimated rideshares are $66, for a projected total of $657. Leave the office around 4:40 p.m. The hotel is cancellable without penalty through 6:00 p.m. Tuesday, May 12.

The flight tickets in both combinations are nonrefundable but may be canceled before departure for airline credit. Nothing has been booked. Once the Thursday ending time is confirmed, the two plans are ready for a final selection.
